mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) indicates inflationary pressures, which typically leads to monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve. This tightening is anticipated to negatively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher interest rates increase the cost of capital.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential slowdown in consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a weakening in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of a broader economic slowdown. This slowdown is expected to negatively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST decreases > 5% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening economy, which is expected to positively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which is expected to negatively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases > 100k MoM and UNRATE increases > 0.2pp MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS decreases > 100k MoM and UNRATE increases > 0.2pp MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which is expected to positively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% MoM for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS increases > 1% MoM for 3 consecutive months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with a decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates a deflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, which is expected to positively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.1% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.1% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a strengthening economy, which is expected to positively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 increases, the hypothesis is rejected.
